document_metadata.document_type: Terms of Service & Legal Notices Portal

jurisdiction_trap.details: Disputes are channeled into individual arbitration via AAA or BBB, or restricted to small claims court in the county of the user's billing address, effectively blocking collective legal action and creating significant logistical barriers.

extracted_clauses.exact_quote: When you use our technologies, you agree to certain terms, which can be found in this section. We also provide you with information about state-specific tariffs, an archive of network disclosures and a guide on our network management principles.
extracted_clauses.plain_english_translation: By merely using our network or visiting our website, you legally bind yourself to our terms. We reserve the right to update these rules at any time, and it is your sole responsibility to hunt through our legal portal to find out how we have changed the deal.

extracted_clauses.exact_quote: YOU AND VERIZON BOTH AGREE TO RESOLVE DISPUTES ONLY BY ARBITRATION OR IN SMALL CLAIMS COURT... YOU ARE GIVING UP THE RIGHT TO GO TO COURT AND HAVE A DISPUTE HEARD BY A JUDGE OR JURY.
extracted_clauses.plain_english_translation: You waive your constitutional right to sue us in a court of law or participate in a class-action lawsuit. If we overcharge you, leak your data, or violate your privacy, you must fight us alone in a private, corporate-friendly arbitration forum.

extracted_clauses.exact_quote: Any feedback, comments, or suggestions you may provide regarding Verizon or the Services is entirely voluntary and we will be free to use such feedback, comments or suggestions as we see fit and without any obligation to you.
extracted_clauses.plain_english_translation: If you submit ideas, feedback, or suggestions on how to improve our services, we take full ownership of those ideas. We can monetize them indefinitely without paying you or giving you credit.

strategic_recommendation: Verizon employs a classic corporate shield architecture designed to eliminate consumer legal recourse. If you must use their services, immediately locate their arbitration opt-out provision (typically required within 30 days of activation) and submit a formal opt-out notice. Otherwise, treat all data passing through their network as subject to corporate telemetry harvesting and assume zero liability on their part for service failures.
